name: Mexican Street Corn Salad (Esquites)
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt offers esquites as the spoonable, less messy alternative to elotes, with the added advantage that it needs no grill. The trick to making it indoors is cutting the kernels off before cooking rather than after, then charring them in a ripping-hot wok or skillet and leaving them undisturbed long enough for the sugars to caramelise and darken before tossing, repeating until they are charred all over; done properly a few kernels pop like popcorn, so a splatter guard is worth having. The hot corn is tossed immediately with the elote flavourings - garlicky mayonnaise, crumbled cotija or feta, scallions, cilantro, jalapeno, lime juice and chile powder - so the dressing clings to each kernel. It is good hot or at room temperature, which makes it a picnic dish.
comment_digest: The highest-voted comments are about serving rather than method: the top one treats it as an appetiser with sturdy tortilla chips, and the next premixes everything but the corn, grills oiled and seasoned cobs, then cuts the kernels straight into the bowl at service. The most common correction is timing, with reviewers reporting the charring takes closer to twice the stated ten minutes and that stirring too often prevents it. Substitutions people report working: frozen corn, which caramelises less but is fine and even makes a decent uncooked cold salad; flat-leaf parsley for cilantro; feta for cotija; minced tinned chipotle in place of chile powder for smoke; and two cans of black beans replacing two ears to make it a main. Sour cream stood in for mayonnaise but did not bind to the hot corn as well. One reader suggests the steps should be reordered so the dressing is made first.
flags: Comments truncated at 'Read More'. Many reviews carry 2026 dates. The recipe gives no quantity for the chile powder, which one reviewer flags.
